instruction:
Turn the following content I sent you into a PPT. Use one slide for each title section, make each level-one heading a section title slide, and place each level-two heading together with its body text. Position level-two headings at the top left of the slide. Include a table of contents slide as well. The title on the opening slide must be “Northern Region Art Paint Sales Growth Plan.” Use SimSun throughout the presentation. (On section title slides, make the text bold, keep it all on one line, and have it fill as much of the line as possible.) Use a green gradient from light to dark for the background throughout the presentation, but do not make the overall color too dark. On body slides, place an orange rectangular border around the text so that the text is enclosed within it; the border must not be so thin that it is difficult to see. Apply different animations to the level-two headings and the body text. Animations on the same slide must play automatically; after moving to a new slide, start its animations with a click. Put the closing section on the final slide. Create the presentation using the template file, and deliver the finished PPT file to me.
I. Market Trends and Consumption Upgrading
1.1 Market Expansion Trend
In 2026, the art paint market remains in a period of rapid expansion. As residents’ home improvement needs shift from “basic living” toward “personalized expression, upgraded texture, and eco-friendly peace of mind,” there is still considerable room for art paint to increase its penetration in the interior wall coatings market.
1.2 Changes in Consumer Demand
Young consumers are gradually becoming the principal decision-makers for home improvement, and they pay greater attention to spatial atmosphere, color coordination, material expression, and an overall sense of design. This shift is moving art paint from a niche decorative material toward a mainstream home improvement category and opening up greater growth potential for wall-aesthetics consumption.
II. Growth Opportunities in Key Cities
2.1 Release of Demand for Housing Upgrades
Market opportunities in key North China cities stem mainly from demand for housing upgrades and existing-home renovation. Following adjustments to real estate policies, transactions in pre-owned homes and demand for upgrade-oriented renovations have been released to some extent in core first-tier cities. Urban renewal projects have also driven demand for wall renovations, upgrades to fully finished interiors, and partial remodeling.
2.2 Existing-Home Renovation Potential
Key cities around the Bohai Rim have considerable potential in the renovation of aging residential communities, the renewal of existing housing, and partial home makeovers. The growth focus of the home furnishing and building materials industry is gradually shifting from incremental new housing toward refined renovation of existing homes. Art paint can use this shift to enter consumption scenarios such as partial makeovers, whole-home renovations, and quality upgrades.
III. Industry Competition and Brand Opportunities
3.1 Changes in the Competitive Landscape
The art paint sector has entered a stage in which brands are intensifying their efforts in a concentrated manner. Leading companies in the industry are competing for consumers’ mindshare through environmental protection systems, product texture, in-store experiences, and designer channels. Some brands have already established a degree of first-mover advantage in both retail and project channels.
3.2 Directions for Brand Breakthrough
Affected by raw materials, environmental standards, and product upgrades, the pricing structure of the coatings industry may continue to adjust. For “Lanting Paint Art,” the window created by upgraded environmental standards and rising aesthetic consumption should be used to strengthen its differentiated advantages in environmental performance, aesthetics, and comprehensive spatial solutions.
IV. Annual Development Goals
4.1 Business Growth Targets
This plan recommends setting the 2026 target for the Northern Region art paint business at year-over-year sales growth of no less than 20%, an increase of 3—5 percentage points in market share in key cities, the addition of approximately 30 art paint specialty stores or shop-in-shops, and an increase of approximately 20% in the number of core dealers.
4.2 Brand Awareness Targets
At the brand level, efforts should focus on establishing the perception that “Lanting Paint Art = Wall Aesthetics Solution Expert,” achieving a marked increase in awareness among target customer groups in key cities, and generating sustained conversion through in-store experiences, designer recommendations, and user word of mouth.
V. Core Product System
5.1 Positioning of the Flagship Series
The core strategy should use the “Artful Home” art paint series as the primary growth engine and the “Color Sensibility in Harmony” coordination system as the link for consumer communication. This system can create color-palette combinations around different living atmospheres, integrating latex paint colors, art paint textures, and spatial styles into a single selection logic.
5.2 Simplifying Consumer Decision-Making
Rather than merely selling individual products, the brand should communicate “a complete wall solution that has already been coordinated” to users. By unifying the expression of color, texture, and style, it can reduce the difficulty consumers face when coordinating art paint selections, allowing users to choose wall effects in the same way they choose a coordinated soft-furnishing set or makeup look.
VI. Product Portfolio and Differentiated Selling Points
6.1 Product Matrix Design
The product strategy should create three portfolio categories: premium products for customer acquisition, mid-range products for sales volume, and products adapted for projects. The premium series can emphasize luminous translucency, delicate textures, and a quiet-luxury style for flagship-store displays and conversion of high-budget customers. The mid-range series can offer art paint combinations at multiple price points and in multiple styles, organized around palettes for different atmospheres. The project series can target fully finished homes, old-property renovation projects, and commercial spaces with product packages better suited to large-scale application, cost control, and consistent results.
6.2 Refining Core Selling Points
Product communications should emphasize core selling points such as leading environmental performance, unified color and texture, professional aesthetic support, and standardized application. Use the combined message of “eco-friendly peace of mind + aesthetic coordination + consistent application” to differentiate the products from ordinary wall materials.
VII. Multichannel Expansion Strategy
7.1 Retail Outlet Upgrade
The channel strategy should be developed along four paths: retail outlets, home improvement companies, contractor groups, and project business. Flagship stores in key cities can undergo an “Artful Home” themed upgrade, with immersive model display zones and color-palette experience zones that allow consumers to see directly how different wall effects appear in real spaces. Shop-in-shops or dedicated art paint areas can be established in building materials markets, supported by samples, color-selection equipment, and sales associate training.
7.2 Home Improvement and Project Channel Expansion
Home improvement companies and designer channels can improve conversion efficiency through strategic partnerships, design salons, model-room placements, and referral incentives. Contractor channels can ensure consistent final execution through training and certification, benchmark recognition, and application support. Project channels should focus on following up on urban renewal, fully finished housing, and commercial space projects, creating dual growth engines in retail and project business.
VIII. Integrated Marketing and Local Conversion
8.1 Online Content Seeding
Marketing should center on content seeding, localized advertising, and city-themed events. Online channels can continuously publish art paint case studies, application processes, before-and-after comparisons, and coordination guides on lifestyle content platforms, short-video platforms, and private-domain communities, creating a closed loop from awareness to inquiry and then to in-store experience.
8.2 Offline Event Conversion
Offline activities in core cities can be built around themes such as “Wall Aesthetics Season,” “Old Home Renewal Festival,” and “Twin-City Year-End Gift.” Promotional approaches can combine existing-customer referrals, residential-community group purchases, completed-home showcase contests, and joint case studies with designers to improve viral reach and local conversion efficiency.
IX. Service System and Implementation Support
9.1 Service System Upgrade
Service and implementation support are crucial to executing the plan. It is recommended to launch an exclusive “Art Paint Renewal” service package covering free on-site surveys, digital color selection, professional application, quality inspection, and post-sale follow-up. For users of existing homes, also provide renovation while occupied, partial renovation, rapid assessment of old walls, and model residential-community services.
9.2 Dealer Empowerment and Organizational Support
Dealers should be provided with product training, sales training, online customer-acquisition training, sample support, store subsidies, and sales incentives. For implementation, the Northern Region can establish a dedicated “Artful Home” working group, with the sales, marketing, channel, training, and project teams collaborating to advance the initiative. Store upgrades, channel expansion, event conversion, and sales attainment should be reviewed monthly to ensure steady achievement of the annual targets.

+3: Slide backgrounds: Use light-to-medium green gradient backgrounds. The overall color is not dark, and the text is clearly readable.

+3: Slide 2, table of contents: A table of contents title and nine level-one table of contents entries are present: “Market Trends and Consumption Upgrading,” “Growth Opportunities in Key Cities,” “Industry Competition and Brand Opportunities,” “Annual Development Goals,” “Core Product System,” “Product Portfolio and Differentiated Selling Points,” “Multichannel Expansion Strategy,” “Integrated Marketing and Local Conversion,” and “Service System and Implementation Support.”

Growth Opportunities in Key Cities,” “III. Industry Competition and Brand Opportunities,” “IV. Annual Development Goals,” “V. Core Product System,” “VI. Product Portfolio and Differentiated Selling Points,” “VII. Multichannel Expansion Strategy,” “VIII. Integrated Marketing and Local Conversion,” and “IX. Service System and Implementation Support.” The text is bold, 38-42 pt, centered in the middle of the slide, and placed on one line.

+5: Slides 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, and 20 are the body slides for Parts I through IX. The level-two headings “1.1 Market Expansion Trend” and “1.2 Changes in Consumer Demand,” “2.1 Release of Demand for Housing Upgrades” and “2.2 Existing-Home Renovation Potential,” “3.1 Changes in the Competitive Landscape” and “3.2 Directions for Brand Breakthrough,” “4.1 Business Growth Targets” and “4.2 Brand Awareness Targets,” “5.1 Positioning of the Flagship Series” and “5.2 Simplifying Consumer Decision-Making,” “6.1 Product Matrix Design” and “6.2 Refining Core Selling Points,” “7.1 Retail Outlet Upgrade” and “7.2 Home Improvement and Project Channel Expansion,” “8.1 Online Content Seeding” and “8.2 Offline Event Conversion,” and “9.1 Service System Upgrade” and “9.2 Dealer Empowerment and Organizational Support” are each positioned in the top-left area of the corresponding section, bold and 16-20 pt. The corresponding body text is placed below each level-two heading, matches that heading, and is 12-16 pt.
+1: Slide 21, closing slide: The closing-slide text uses SimSun and may include “Thank You for Watching” and “Northern Region Art Paint Sales Growth Plan”; it must not include any unrelated topic.

+3: Orange rectangular borders on all body slides: Every body slide has an orange rectangular border around its text, enclosing the level-two headings and body text. The rectangular border is an editable shape with a clearly visible outline. The orange rectangular border has a line width of approximately 1.5—3 pt and is orange or dark orange; it must not be so thin that it is difficult to distinguish.
+3: Font throughout the presentation: All visible Chinese text uses SimSun, including the table of contents, titles, level-two headings, body text, footers, and closing-slide text.
+5: Level-two heading animations on body slides: Every level-two heading on Slides 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, and 20 uses an animation effect.

+5: Body-text animations on body slides: All body text on Slides 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, and 20 has animations applied, and these animations are clearly distinct from the level-two heading animations.

+5: Animation triggers on body slides: After entering each body slide, a click starts that slide’s animations, after which the level-two headings and body text appear automatically in sequence on the same slide.

+3: Animation order on body slides: On each body slide, a level-two heading appears before its corresponding body text, and the animation sequence of the two level-two subsections matches the order of the text on the slide.

+3: Animation continuity on body slides: Animations on the same slide are set to “After Previous” or an equivalent automatic playback setting; the user does not need to click repeatedly multiple times to view all content on the slide.

+3: Difference between animation effects: Level-two headings may use effects such as Fade, Fly In, or Wipe, while body text uses a different effect. All objects must not use exactly the same animation.
+3: Slide transition logic: After moving to a new slide, its animations do not play automatically in advance; a click is required to start the content animations on that slide.
